comparator.name: Medicine
comparator.sourceNotes: Groningen combines the causes of disease and medical knowledge with training in consultation, professional practice, healthy ageing and research. This plan illustrates the Sustainable Care learning community. Students prepare their bachelor project in the first semester of year three and carry it out in the final semester.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 1.1 — Development and Metabolic Diseases
components.note: Integrated basic and clinical medicine.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 1.2 — Endocrine Regulation, Blood and Neoplasms
components.note: Integrated basic and clinical medicine.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 1.3 — Infection and Immune System
components.note: Integrated basic and clinical medicine.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 1.4 — Ischemia
components.note: Integrated basic and clinical medicine.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 1.5 — Trauma (ABCDE)
components.note: Integrated basic and clinical medicine.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 1.6 — Degeneration, Vulnerability and Disease
components.note: Integrated basic and clinical medicine.

components.name: Knowledge Development B1
components.note: Four longitudinal interfaculty medical progress tests.

components.name: Competency Development 1.1 — Sustainable Care
components.note: Professional development, medical consultation, healthy ageing and scientific training in the selected Learning Community.

components.name: Competency Development 1.2 — Sustainable Care
components.note: Professional development, medical consultation, healthy ageing and scientific training in the selected Learning Community.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 2.1 — Systemic diseases
components.note: Study disease processes affecting multiple organ systems.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 2.2 — Shortness of breath and fatigue
components.note: Study heart failure, lung disease and several cancers, including their effects on patients.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 2.3 — Digestive tract and neoplasms
components.note: Study digestive disorders and tumours in an integrated medical block.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 2.4 — Endocrinology and reproduction
components.note: Study hormonal disorders and reproductive medicine.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 2.5 — Women’s and children’s health
components.note: Study health and disease in women and children.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 2.6 — Growth and development
components.note: Study growth and development and related disorders.

components.name: Knowledge Development B2
components.note: Four longitudinal interfaculty medical progress tests.

components.name: Competency Development 2.1 — Sustainable Care
components.note: Clinical and professional competency development in the selected Learning Community.

components.name: Competency Development 2.2 — Sustainable Care
components.note: Clinical and professional competency development in the selected Learning Community.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 3.1 — Sensation and movement
components.note: Study the peripheral nervous system, senses, movement and pain.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 3.2 — Brain and cognition
components.note: Study neurological presentations including movement disorders, dementia and delirium.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 3.3 — Psychiatric health and disease
components.note: Study mood, anxiety and psychotic disorders alongside other psychiatric conditions.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 3.4 — Acute medicine I
components.note: Study acute presentations and the foundations of emergency care.

components.name: Causes of Diseases 3.5 — Acute medicine II
components.note: Continue the study of acute medical presentations and care.

components.name: Knowledge Development B3
components.note: Four longitudinal interfaculty medical progress tests.

components.name: Competency Development 3.1 — Sustainable Care
components.note: Develop an approved proposal for the bachelor project while continuing the competency training.

components.name: Competency Development 3.2
components.note: Carry out research in a small team. Each student writes a thesis and reflection and takes part in the final presentation. The project is included in this 20 EC block.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic Medicine target offers four Learning Communities for the Competency Development components while retaining one common medical-knowledge curriculum. Current official evidence does not identify one community as the broad default or academically dominant route. Sustainable Care is therefore selected neutrally because it is listed first in the 2026-2027 TER, without reference to UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three related fields offer substantive, distinct responses to Groningen Medicine. Biomedical science has the strongest scientific overlap. Health psychology studies illness experience and interaction, and population health studies prevention and inequality. The professional and clinical curriculum remains a separate feature of Medicine.

notes.text: Groningen teaches medicine through biological science, clinical reasoning, medical consultation and supervised care. The UCR options explore related academic fields and do not lead to physician qualification.

The UCR options do not include supervised patient care, clinical examination and treatment training, or Groningen’s medical progress tests. Groningen’s required bachelor project is assessed within its final competency block.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen Medicine studies the causes of disease and prepares students for medical practice through consultation training, supervised care and research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore disease mechanisms, health behaviour and population health. Groningen combines these subjects with training and assessment in clinical practice.

cellNotes.text: Both study neoplasms and processes underlying disease. Groningen also covers endocrine and blood disorders in clinical context.
Both study pathogens, immune responses and infection. Groningen integrates those topics with medical cases.
Both cover disease mechanisms in the heart and lungs. Groningen also studies clinical presentations and care.
Both study brain function, including consciousness and cognitive processes. Groningen focuses on neurological presentations.
Both examine mood, anxiety and psychotic disorders. Groningen integrates the material with medical and psychiatric practice.
